subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the Hardy-Weinberg equations, q squared represents the frequency of:
questions.explain: q squared is the frequency of the homozygous recessive genotype, since q is the recessive allele frequency.

questions.q: Which genus of bacteria fixes nitrogen within the root nodules of leguminous plants?
questions.explain: Rhizobium lives mutualistically in legume root nodules and fixes atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia.

questions.q: In which part of the chloroplast do the light-dependent reactions take place?
questions.explain: The light-dependent reactions occur on the thylakoid membranes, where the photosystems are embedded.

questions.q: Modern classification places organisms into three domains. These are:
questions.explain: The three-domain system divides life into Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya based largely on rRNA sequence differences.

questions.q: Which process in the nitrogen cycle returns nitrogen gas to the atmosphere, reducing soil fertility?
questions.explain: Denitrifying bacteria in anaerobic soils convert nitrate back to nitrogen gas, lowering soil nitrogen.

questions.q: Out of every six molecules of triose phosphate (TP) made in the Calvin cycle, how many are used to regenerate RuBP?
questions.explain: Five of every six TP molecules are recycled to regenerate RuBP, leaving one to contribute to carbohydrate.

questions.q: In a graph of photosynthesis rate against light intensity, what does a plateau region indicate?
options: A factor other than light, such as CO2 or temperature, is now limiting
questions.explain: Once the curve plateaus, increasing light has no effect, so another factor limits the rate.

questions.q: The Hardy-Weinberg principle predicts that allele and genotype frequencies remain constant only if:
options: The population is small with frequent migration
There is no mutation, no selection, no migration, random mating and a large population
questions.explain: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium assumes a large population with no mutation, selection or migration and random mating.

questions.q: Which statement correctly summarises where the two main stages of photosynthesis occur?
options: Light-dependent in the thylakoids; light-independent in the stroma
Both stages occur in the stroma
Light-dependent in the stroma; light-independent in the thylakoids
Both stages occur on the thylakoid membranes
questions.explain: The light reactions occur on the thylakoid membranes and the Calvin cycle occurs in the stroma.

questions.q: How does cyclic photophosphorylation differ from non-cyclic photophosphorylation?
options: It produces oxygen but no ATP
It uses photosystem II only and reduces NADP
It occurs in the stroma and fixes carbon dioxide
It involves only photosystem I and produces ATP but no reduced NADP
questions.explain: In cyclic flow, electrons from photosystem I return to it, generating ATP without photolysis or reduced NADP.

questions.q: A producer has a GPP of 20,000 kJ per m2 per yr and respiratory losses of 8,000 kJ per m2 per yr. What is its NPP?
questions.explain: NPP = GPP - respiration = 20,000 - 8,000 = 12,000 kJ per m2 per yr.

A community held at a stage before the natural climax by human activity such as grazing
The earliest pioneer stage of succession
